entities.summary:
Publius Manilius Vopiscus Vicinillianus was a Roman senator who served as ordinary consul for the year 114 AD, alongside Quintus Ninnius Hasta. This marked a pivotal moment in the Late Republic and early Imperial periods, as the Principate began to emerge from the ashes of the Roman Republic. As consul, Publius Manilius played a key role in shaping the governance and politics of Rome during this critical era. His tenure also highlighted the complexities of Roman politics, the rise of the Principate, and the gradual shift from the Roman Republic to the Roman Empire.

The significance of Publius Manilius Vopiscus Vicinillianus lies in his contributions to the development of the Roman governance and politics, which had far-reaching consequences for the Roman Empire. His life and career serve as a microcosm of the larger trends and events shaping the Late Republic and early Imperial periods. As a senator, Publius Manilius participated in the intricate web of Roman politics, navigating the complexities of the Roman governance and its impact on the Roman people.

The legacy of Publius Manilius Vopiscus Vicinillianus can be seen in the emergence of the Principate, which marked a significant turning point in Roman history. His role in shaping the governance and politics of Rome during this critical era had a lasting impact on the Roman Empire, shaping its development and trajectory for centuries to come.

In the annals of Roman history, Publius Manilius Vopiscus Vicinillianus stands as a testament to the complexities and nuances of Roman politics during the Late Republic and early Imperial periods. His life and career serve as a reminder of the enduring power of human agency and the intricate web of historical forces that shape the course of human civilization.
